entities.name: Peritumoral flow velocity v0
observations: Pretreatment outward peritumoral interstitial fluid flow velocity measured by Gd-DTPA DCE-MRI was associated with disease-free and overall survival in cervical carcinoma cohorts.
Higher v0 was associated with poorer disease-free and overall survival; it retained independent prognostic information in multivariable analyses in the reported cohorts.

entities.name: Cervical carcinoma
observations: Two small human observational cohorts evaluated pretreatment DCE-MRI-derived peritumoral flow velocity in patients treated with cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy.

entities.name: v0 predicts cervical survival
observations: In a 62-patient stage IB–IIIB cohort, v0 was associated with disease-free and overall survival and was the only independent prognostic variable among stage, tumor volume, and lymph-node status.

In a 54-patient cohort, high v0 was associated with poor disease-free and overall survival; high v0 plus large low-enhancing tumor volume corresponded to 13% 5-year DFS/OS versus 100% with low v0 plus small low-enhancing volume.
Evidence is limited to small observational cohorts; treatment-independent causality, external validation, and precise effect sizes were not established.
